title: The First Planting Week

arc.title: The Cold Stone
arc.subtitle: a warm stone, already going cold

epigraph.text: Sow with the hand and count with the hand; the slate lies in the sun and takes no seed. A strip is a direction until somebody puts a back into it, and a direction has no figure to be entered.
epigraph.attribution: A saying of the seed-grounds east of Low Kiln

pov: Daniel Marchetti (Corin), close third-person past tense inside a ninety-one-to-ninety-three-day-old body carried everywhere; the old life colours the noticing (a count kept exactly against a house that keeps it badly, the order of the hand to the record before the person, an anatomy read perfectly and worth nothing) without a present-tense Chicago break or a \memory{} tag --- the old life stays offstage --- and there is no departure from his eyes, no Court, Waiting Room or collector interior

scenes.title: A Direction, Not a Number
scenes.synopsis: One dated entry, Day 91, Seed 2, Secondday, morning in the strips east of Low Kiln on the barley fields and back to the Clay Yard and the Vail kiln-house. The first planting work begins on the ground the boy had carried only as a direction: brooms and glances, seed counted in handfuls and looks, no figure spoken. The strips want hands and nobody gives a number for the hands or the strips. Berr Clay comes down short with the red wool cord folded under his coat, green of tasted glaze at a mouth, a figure he will not give and the true subtraction unspoken, taking himself out of his own sentence with the slate-at-the-watch grammar. Sella gives the broom its instruction before anybody and never gives one to the basket; the boy, ninety-one days old and carried at the edge, keeps the count exactly while the house keeps it badly in loaves, glances and a space nobody names. One brown-edged crust lies stiff in the fold with the empty place beside it still unnamed and no third; the new finer grey in the Vail corner is still unswept and called the thaw; the carried fire keeps four, four and a gap under blind ash with its payer unnamed. Change: a direction becomes worked ground and seed goes into it, but the arithmetic stays unchanged --- the count goes on exact. Advances T071/T072 (91), T077, T041/T047, T009/T013/T092, T058/T079, T060/T086, T088. Withheld: no figure for hands or strips, no number spoken, no joining of the direction to a number, no seventh hearing, no ending.

scenes.title: Ask the Pot
scenes.synopsis: One dated entry, Day 91, Seed 2, Secondday, midday at the yard well and drying racks, dusk under the Vail kiln-house roof. A woman asks what the planting will cost now that seed is in the ground; Sella moves her lips along the loaf shelf, glances at the clay jar, leaves the space at the row's end with no figure and tells her to ask the pot what a wet thing costs set down there and that the house has said it. The boy wants the number of his days spoken by somebody who would know what it counted and nobody speaks it. The private file is checked and unchanged: six hearings of the full note stay six from four sources plus the one from a person, beside and never among, no seventh; three near-full answers stand advanced and not paid; three intervals on another tray; the word forty a saying with the readable double turn beside it and the weight of a thumb apart; four low sounds in four places with the river's note a fifth; the two tellings of the shut room on their own tray joined to no kiln; the loan that can hear uncalled; the cold foot below the sill still the cold to one woman and weather to the yard, uncured and unnamed. The body humiliates him exactly: frozen drool unwiped, head going where it wants, cold cheek-temple-wrist with the wool riding back, the hand up an inch toward the note of water going over water and down. Sella tells the fire it is the thaw and touches the widow's mark at no hour, because no opening came. Advances T071/T072, T060/T086, T092/T013, T088, T061/T082, T065/T095, T076, T093/T094, T058/T079. Withheld: no figure, no name for the empty place, no cause written across the trays, no ending.

scenes.title: Grey Past the Bent Finger
scenes.synopsis: One dated entry, Day 92, Seed 3, Thirdday, before light through midday at the Vail wheel-shed and its damper, under the Vail roof at dusk. Jorra comes through the finger's-width-open wheel-shed door with fine grey slate dust worked into both forearms past the bend of his little finger, not bone-coloured slip; men came in since first light and spoke low in the back room and he gives the house no name for them. The broken birth-slates stay under the lowest rack, gone around as wide as a pail of hot water set where a child might knock it and entered by nobody. He speaks to the wheel before anyone --- it does not care whose hands, only if they are steady --- tells a pot it will do, knows the full note of a Vail pot before it leaves the wheel and will not say so before a kiln-master from High Kiln. When Sella has not finished telling him the fire is low, his bent finger goes into the damper ahead of her sentence, the cold iron taking the cold out of his fingertip, so the end of her instruction arrives at the pot and the household straightens around his silence; he reads the damper as any iron that stops a thing from running, the same bite that keeps a vessel whole can take the hand off a man, and no Grathic word holds both mercies. He does not say the back room is cold and does not look toward the bed or the basket. He's not Vail stays sealed and the promise of the foundling's name to the men who burn slates is neither given nor withdrawn. Advances T035/T031, T061, T057/T084, T058/T079, T071/T072 (92). Withheld: no name or number from the back room, no slate examined, no name given, no ending.

scenes.title: Six Counted
scenes.synopsis: One dated entry, Day 92, Seed 3, Thirdday, before light through dusk in the Clay Yard and under the Vail roof. Tarn sets the small bench knife on its sill before the light and tells the sill first and the yard after where it is, six years standing in a mark his thumb has worn almost flat and the seventh never cut, nearly gone and still held, the one entry in this house the house cannot check. To the kindling: Six counted. The next I don't count. Ash is worked into the creases of his knuckles in the colour of the clean dark line and no scrubbing lifts it; the pale clip-ring at his left wrist holds what light there is and gives it back. He says Yes, house to the early thaw and the late, agrees so entirely that no argument can find a foot, and keeps wanting the late because it puts off the paying, though the paying has stood in the ruts since the water went. His broom goes over the road a house sends a man down when it wants a collector, over and over, without once turning along it; he was sent once in the Long Cold and came back at the frozen ford and told the house it had been done, and keeps that sentence where he keeps the seventh year. A vessel gives its note past the door and his head does not turn and he does not name the sound; the boy does not call it a seventh hearing, and two ears and two silences keep their equality under one roof with the loan that can hear still uncalled. Something must give at the end of the seventh year and it does not give here. Advances T036 (do not pay), T076, T009/T090, T061/T082, T071/T072 (92), T088. Withheld: no spending of the seventh year, no calling of the loan, no seventh hearing, no ending.

scenes.title: The Landing Out of Line
scenes.synopsis: One dated entry, Day 93, Seed 4, Fourthday, dawn market through afternoon at the Fishstairs below the north bridge, back under the Vail roof at dusk. Sella sets the basket at the edge of the fish-trade shade where no slate lies and gives the instruction to the wool and the water, never to the basket. Mira Silt works the eels with pale slime dried on her sleeves, silt in the hollow of her neck and her head held where the top of her left ear had been, her small smile kept like a door on the latch; asked whether the run will be thin she answers the question with her own, Thin? Who's to say thin? It comes when it comes. Ask the river, and moves eel-bones against her thumb while deciding whether to lie. When a buyer names a figure her thumb goes under her apron to the grey cord and stays; shifting a creel shows the second cord twisted twice beneath it, never carried upriver to Nine Pots or lifted at a door, neither knot counted and the knot for the thin child upriver untouched. Her board lies beside Orra's knot-string and does not touch it; Orra stays offstage watching and gets no answer. The steps come back four, four and a landing a hand's breadth out of line that a whole market walks carefully over without a fall, and word comes that the weak board at the Weir is gone or trodden flat and nobody has gone down to see which. The soft-cuffed clerk still sits at the landing with his slate to his forearm for a measure nobody called, hand to slate before eyes to stalls, filed apart from Marra, the Drawing collector and the Court-table clerk with no sixth sighting of the neat dark hand. The boy sets Mira's not-looking, a keeping, beside Berr's not-looking, a pricing, in places that do not touch. Advances T059/T025/T024, T090/T080, T083, T058/T079, T071/T072 (93). Withheld: no knot counted, no door knocked at Nine Pots, no fall made of the step or the board, no sixth sighting, no ending.

scenes.title: Warm and Breathing
scenes.synopsis: One dated entry, Day 93, Seed 4, Fourthday, midday three doors down in House Silt and dusk under the Vail kiln-house roof. Sella sets the basket just inside the finger's-width-open door at the edge of the light away from every open slate, opens no slate and turns no errand into a walk to Slate Row. Alda Reed comes short with soap-and-milk gone cold under river silt and lye sour under the soap, nails scrubbed to the quick with clay still under them; she lays her birth-slates writing-down on the bench before she turns to the fold, presses the fold a breath too long, crosses two fingers at the red edge of the birth-flower before she knows it and covers the sign with the date she gave Dessa, a woman more mornings dead than any living person keeps count of. To Sella's he lies quiet she says Warm and breathing, that's all I've set down, exact and not true, and goes on with dates after the question has stopped. Her hand goes once to the little tin in her bodice without opening it; her sixth narrow slate stays turned face-down toward a floorboard in a house the boy cannot name, six pages all unread, no seventh written and T023 not paid again. Above the abandoned board-bed the round pewter tin keeps its pale fold and thumb-bright rub unopened, and the grey wool below holds only the hollow where the small pale river stone lay; nobody says either is gone. Two private records in two materials stand apart in one room, read by nobody and carried to no door. At dusk home, the private file is checked and unchanged: six hearings stay six beside and never among, three near-full answers advanced and not paid, word unspoken, the two tellings on their tray, the loan uncalled, one stiff crust in the fold with the empty place unnamed and no third. Sella sets him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without looking at his face and leaves the thread frozen; the river's note from the Ilm comes through the finger's-width-open door and the fire's four, four and a gap through the floor, the two sounds in two separate places. His hand goes up an inch toward the water and comes down; the count crosses into Day 94 unspent. Advances T023 (carried, not repaid), T089/T074, T007/T008/T073, T081, T061/T082, T086/T060, T058/T079, T071/T072 (93). Withheld: no name or number from Dessa, no tin opened, no recognition, no seventh page, no seventh hearing, no ending.
